Horadric Odds

D2R drop calculator
Welcome to Horadric Odds — a free, fan-made Diablo II: Resurrected toolkit.
  1. Drop odds: search any item (nicknames like "shako" work) to see which monsters drop it and your chance per kill at your difficulty, players and magic find.
  2. Build planner: open Share & Library, pick a starter build or make your own, and spend points on Skills & Stats.
  3. Play it: the Leveling Guide has a checklist to tick off while you level, and Gear shows where to farm each item.
What's new · 4 Nov 2026: New Experience tab: kills to your next level, the best places to level and terror zone experience. Share builds as links (Share & Library → Copy share link). Also fixed odds for magic items with sockets (Jeweler's and Artificer's affixes) in drops and gambling.
About & credits

Horadric Odds is free and fan-made. It isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard Entertainment, Maxroll, IGN, Icy Veins or Traderie. Diablo II: Resurrected and its game data belong to Blizzard Entertainment.

Game data: items, drop tables, skill trees and formulas come from the game files via blizzhackers/d2data (MIT License, © 2020 blizzhackers).

Experience: rules checked against The Amazon Basin wiki; monster counts per area are the estimates in blizzhackers/d2data. Attack frames: animation frame data and timing rules follow Warren1001's IAS Calculator (animation tables dumped by RuffnecKk). Cast, hit-recovery and block breakpoints: d2runewizard, with the Warlock tables confirmed against AOEAH.

Builds: starter builds are written for Horadric Odds from the game data and common community knowledge. Full guides by Maxroll and Icy Veins are linked from each build and from the Guides list. Share builds as links or build codes from Share & Library.

Prices: price links open Traderie's own pages; Horadric Odds doesn't collect or store Traderie data.

Bugs and ideas: open an issue on GitHub or email the address below.

Contact, problems or takedown requests: email HoradricOdds@hotmail.com.

Magic find, difficulty and players don't affect gambling.

      How it works. Odds are calculated from the game's own drop tables (treasure classes, monster levels, item ratios), following the in-game rules: NoDrop scaling by player count, the level-based treasure class upgrade in Nightmare and Hell, nested picks with the 6-item limit per kill, the quality roll with diminishing magic find, and unique/set selection by rarity. Chances are per kill. With Find Item they're per successful search. Stat rolls: every value in a stat's range is equally likely; magic and rare affixes follow the game's affix level, weights, group and prefix/suffix rules.

      Game versions. D2R Reign of the Warlock (current), D2R before the expansion (patches 2.4 to 2.9) and Lord of Destruction 1.14d (same drop tables as 1.13c). Classic LoD tables come from the game's 1.14d patch files; item and skill names are shared with D2R.

      Compared with Silospen. Same maths: regular monsters, cows and champions match exactly. Checked against all three of its game versions. Bosses at 1 player and the Countess's runes differ because Silospen approximates the 6-items-per-kill limit (it counts only 6 of a boss's 7 picks and doesn't limit nested picks), while this calculator applies the limit as the game does.

      Gambling follows the rules published on Blizzard's Arreat Summit (item level, upgrade chances, fixed quality odds); the elite upgrade is assumed to be checked before the exceptional one.

      Sharing. The page's link keeps the item, stats and settings you picked, so copying it shares your exact calculation.

      Not modelled. The once-per-game unique rule, scripted drops (Cow King hide, organs from Uber events, Hellfire Torch, Annihilus) and super uniques without a fixed location. Heralds are assumed to get the same +3 level bonus as unique monsters.

      Data: game tables via blizzhackers/d2data (MIT). Open source under the MIT License. Diablo is a trademark of Blizzard Entertainment; this is a fan tool, not affiliated with Blizzard.

      How it works. Experience follows the game's rules: monster base experience by level, the player count bonus (+50% per extra player), the party bonus and level-based split, the level difference penalty, the high-level reduction from level 70 and the 8,388,607 per-kill cap. Champions give 3× (berserkers 5×), uniques, minions and super uniques 5×. Clears use the game data's estimated monster counts for each area, with 3 champions per pack and 3–6 minions per unique, so treat them as averages. Baal's five waves are counted, but each wave is treated as its boss plus that boss's minion type, so the Throne numbers are close rather than exact. Not counted: monsters that appear mid-fight (Fallen revived by Shamans, Vile Children from Vile Mothers and the like), because how many you get depends on how you play, and the one-time reward from the Ancients quest, since it can't be farmed. Data from blizzhackers/d2data (MIT); rules checked against The Amazon Basin wiki.
